¿PORQUÉ ES IMPORTANTE OPTIMIZAR LAS IMÁGENES DE UN SITIO WEB?

Optimizar las imágenes de un sitio web es crucial porque reduce el peso de los archivos sin perder calidad visual. Esto acelera la carga de la página, mejora el posicionamiento SEO en Google, optimiza la experiencia del usuario (lo que aumenta las conversiones y ventas) y ahorra espacio en el servidor.

El proceso de optimización se divide en tres pilares principales:

Tamaño y dimensiones: Ajustar la imagen a las medidas exactas (en píxeles) en las que se va a mostrar, evitando subir imágenes inmensas que la web solo reducirá visualmente.

Compresión: Reducir el peso en kilobytes (KB o MB) utilizando herramientas de compresión para que el navegador del usuario descargue la imagen mucho más rápido.

Formatos adecuados: Usar formatos modernos como WebP para fotografías, o PNG/SVG para logotipos e íconos con fondos transparentes.

Las imágenes sin optimizar son la causa principal de los sitios web lentos. Esto genera tasas de rebote más altas (usuarios que abandonan la página antes de que cargue) y penalizaciones por parte de los motores de búsqueda.


¿QUÉ ES SHORTPIXEL?

ShortPixel es un plugin y herramienta en la nube que comprime y optimiza imágenes y archivos PDF para sitios web. Su objetivo principal es reducir drásticamente el peso de los archivos de manera automática y convertirlos a formatos de última generación como WebP y AVIF, logrando que las páginas carguen mucho más rápido y mejorando el posicionamiento SEO.


¿CUÁLES SON LAS CARACTERÍSTICAS Y BENEFICIOS DE SHORTPIXEL?


  • Compresión avanzada: Ofrece tres modos: Lossy (máxima reducción con pérdida de calidad casi imperceptible), Glossy (alta calidad visual) y Lossless (sin pérdida de calidad).

  • Mejora del rendimiento del sitio web : Transforma automáticamente tus archivos JPEG, PNG o GIF a formatos ligeros como WebP y AVIF.

  • Optimización en lote: Permite comprimir la biblioteca de medios existente de una sola vez.

  • Compatibilidad: Aunque destaca principalmente en WordPress, se puede utilizar en cualquier CMS mediante su API o directamente desde su web para subidas manuales.

Protect adults at risk with confidence

Would you know how to respond if an adult disclosed abuse, neglect or exploitation? Could you recognise the less obvious signs of financial abuse, coercive control, organisational abuse, modern slavery or online exploitation?

Safeguarding concerns are not always obvious, and responding incorrectly can place an adult at greater risk. Professionals and volunteers need more than basic awareness—they need the confidence to recognise concerns, respond appropriately, record information accurately and report it through the correct channels.

This Safeguarding Adults and Vulnerable People course provides practical, UK-focused training for anyone who supports, cares for or works alongside adults at risk. Rather than focusing solely on policies, the course connects legal responsibilities with practical workplace actions, helping you move confidently from recognising a concern to taking appropriate, person-centred action.

Understanding adults at risk

Learn what safeguarding means, who may be at risk, and how factors such as disability, illness, mental health needs, isolation, age, dependency and power imbalances can affect a person’s ability to stay safe. Explore the key principles that support effective safeguarding practice.

Recognising abuse and exploitation

Understand different forms of abuse, including physical, sexual, emotional, financial and discriminatory abuse, neglect, domestic abuse, modern slavery, radicalisation and online exploitation. Learn to recognise possible warning signs and understand your responsibility to record and report concerns.

Understanding UK safeguarding responsibilities

Explore key UK safeguarding legislation and guidance, including the Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005, duty of care, information sharing, Prevent duty and multi-agency working.

Responding to disclosures

Learn how to respond calmly and professionally when someone discloses abuse. Practise listening without judgement, avoiding leading questions, recording the person’s own words and reporting concerns promptly.

Recording and reporting concerns

Develop the skills to create clear, accurate and objective safeguarding records, including observations, disclosures, dates, actions taken and relevant facts.

Building a proactive safeguarding culture

Discover how professional curiosity, early intervention, trauma-informed practice, whistleblowing and person-centred support help create safer environments.

courseDetails.title: Horse Colic: Emergency Management & Life-Saving Decisions
courseDetails.shortDescription: Recognize, diagnose, and manage horse colic with confidence—practical, real-world strategies for vets, students, and hor
courseDetails.longDescription:
Colic is one of the most common and life-threatening conditions affecting horses, requiring rapid recognition, accurate diagnosis, and decisive management. This course, “Horse Colic: Emergency Management & Life-Saving Decisions for Equine Care,” is designed to equip learners with the essential knowledge and practical skills needed to confidently approach colic cases in real-world situations.

Rather than focusing only on theory, this course takes a clinical, problem-solving approach, guiding you through how veterinarians think and act when faced with a colic emergency. You will begin by understanding the true meaning of colic as a clinical syndrome, exploring its wide range of causes and varying levels of severity.

A strong foundation is built through a clear explanation of the equine gastrointestinal anatomy and physiology, highlighting the unique features that make horses particularly susceptible to colic. From the small stomach and inability to vomit, to the complex structure of the large colon and common sites of obstruction such as the pelvic flexure, each concept is presented in a simple and practical way.

The course also emphasizes the importance of fluid dynamics, ingesta movement, and the role of bacterial endotoxins, helping you understand why some cases rapidly deteriorate and become life-threatening.

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

  • Recognize early and advanced signs of colic

  • Understand the underlying causes and risk factors

  • Apply structured clinical thinking to assess cases

  • Make informed decisions about treatment and referral

This course is ideal for veterinary students, equine practitioners, horse owners, and anyone involved in horse care who wants to improve their confidence and competence in handling colic cases.

Whether you are preparing for clinical practice or aiming to enhance your field skills, this course provides practical, actionable knowledge that can make a real difference in equine health and survival.
